insights.concise_text: Because instructors cannot monitor all student discussions, the paper frames instructor intervention prediction as binary classification to aid selective intervention.

triple.subject: inability to monitor all student discussions
triple.object: binary classification for selective instructor intervention

insights.concise_text: The attention models proposed to infer latent context are evaluated on a corpus of 12 MOOC discussion forums.

triple.subject: attention models
triple.object: a corpus of 12 MOOC discussion forums

insights.concise_text: Because the actual instructor intervention is unavailable at decision timing, UPA uses the most recent content in the thread as the attentional query for context.

triple.subject: unavailable actual instructor intervention
triple.object: UPA to use the most recent content in the thread as the attentional query for context

insights.concise_text: The UPA and PPA attention models better the vanilla hLSTM by 5% and 2% on average in INLINEFORM0, supporting the claim that context inference improves intervention prediction.

triple.subject: UPA and PPA attention models
triple.object: vanilla hLSTM by 5% and 2% on average in INLINEFORM0

insights.concise_text: APA's relaxation to any previous post as a query is consistent with its better prediction on longer threads, which possess more candidate contexts.

triple.subject: APA
triple.object: context inference to any previous post and predicts intervention on longer threads better

insights.concise_text: UPA's overall best performance is explained by its strength on shorter threads and the corpus having most interventions after one post.

triple.subject: most interventions after one post
triple.object: UPA's overall best performance despite weaker longer-thread performance

insights.concise_text: The paper's hierarchical LSTM basis uses hidden unit outputs as contexts, which the attention models selectively infer instead of using the complete thread.

triple.subject: hierarchical LSTM (hLSTM) model
triple.object: attention models that selectively infer contexts from hidden unit outputs

insights.concise_text: Because Coursera forums do not provide reply structure, the proposed hierarchical model infers reply structure using an attention mechanism.

triple.subject: Coursera forums lacking reply structure
triple.object: a hierarchical model that infers reply structure using an attention mechanism

insights.concise_text: The evaluation's emphasis on recall of the positive class aligns with the claim that missing an intervention is costlier than false positives.

triple.subject: recall of the positive class
triple.object: evaluation priority because missing an intervention is costlier than false positives
